title: How do planes fly?
examples: What parts of the wing make the plane go up?
Are the four forces always balanced when a plane flies straight?
Does the speed of the plane change the forces?

explain.say: Today we are learning about how airplanes stay up in the air.
First we look at lift, which is the upward force on the wings.
The shape of the wing is very important for creating lift.
Next is weight, which is the force pulling the plane down.
Thrust is the forward force created by the engines pushing air back.
Drag is the resistance force that slows the plane down as it moves.

faq.q: If lift is up and weight is down, what must happen for the plane to fly?
faq.a: For the plane to maintain a constant altitude, the lift force must balance the weight force. You could also ask what keeps the plane level, or what force must equal gravity.
asks: How do lift and weight relate?

faq.q: Do I need thrust to create lift?
faq.a: No, lift is created by the wing shape moving through the air, not directly by the engines. Other ways to ask this are what powers the lift, or does the engine make the lift?
asks: Is the engine the source of lift?

faq.q: When does drag become the most important force?
faq.a: Drag becomes very important when the plane is moving very fast or through thick air. Students might ask what slows the plane down, or when is resistance highest?

faq.q: Does the wing shape only matter for lift?
faq.a: The shape affects lift, but it also affects drag, making the plane more or less efficient. You could ask how shape affects drag, or what makes the wing cut through air well?
asks: Is the wing shape important for drag too?
What is the role of the wing shape?

faq.q: If I increase my speed, what happens to the forces?
faq.a: Increasing speed increases both lift and drag, but they increase in different ways. You might ask how speed affects the forces, or what happens to drag at high speed?
asks: Does speed help lift or hurt it?
How do speed and drag interact?

facts: Lift is generated by the difference in air pressure over the curved top and flatter bottom of the wing.
Weight is the force of gravity pulling the entire mass of the plane toward the Earth.
Thrust is the forward force provided by the engines or propellers.
Drag is the force that opposes the motion of the plane through the air.

quiz.say: For a plane flying at a constant speed and altitude, which relationship between the four forces is correct?
quiz.why: When the plane is steady, the upward force (lift) must exactly balance the downward force (weight), and the forward force (thrust) must balance the backward force (drag).

wrong.0: Adding all forces together does not correctly represent the opposing pairs of forces.
wrong.2: This only considers vertical forces and ignores the horizontal forces of thrust and drag.
wrong.3: This only considers horizontal forces and ignores the vertical forces of lift and weight.

quiz.say: If a plane needs to climb upwards, which force must become greater than its opposite?

options.show: Lift must be greater than Thrust
options.say: Lift must be greater than Thrust

options.show: Lift must be greater than Weight
options.say: Lift must be greater than Weight

options.show: Weight must be greater than Lift
options.say: Weight must be greater than Lift

options.show: Thrust must be greater than Drag
options.say: Thrust must be greater than Drag

quiz.why: To move upwards, the upward force (lift) must overcome the downward force (weight).

wrong.0: Lift and thrust are different forces acting in different directions.
wrong.2: If weight were greater than lift, the plane would fall to the ground.
wrong.3: While this is needed for speed, it does not determine if the plane is climbing or falling.

quiz.say: What happens to the forces if the plane suddenly loses engine power?

options.show: Thrust becomes zero, and drag and weight remain.
options.say: Thrust becomes zero, and drag and weight remain.

quiz.why: Without engine power, thrust drops to zero, but gravity (weight) and air resistance (drag) are still acting on the plane.

wrong.1: Lift depends on speed and shape, not just the engines, so it does not vanish instantly.
wrong.2: Drag is caused by the air resistance, which is still present even if the engines stop.
wrong.3: Weight is due to gravity, which continues to pull the plane down regardless of engine power.
